newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX gains 1.5 pct at start but Siemens weak.
newsitem.headline: German DAX gains 1.5 pct at start but Siemens weak.

text.p: Germany's DAX share index rose at the start of bourse trade on Wednesday after the Dow's overnight gains but could not match the jump in U.S. stocks as profits from index-heavyweight Siemens AG disappoint.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shasres rose 52.43 points to 3,392.76 in early bourse trade, with June DAX futures up 37 points to 3,399.0. The Dow overnight had raced 2.60 percent ahead.

Shares in Siemens fell 90 pfennigs to 90 marks in pre-bourse trade immediately after it published 1996/97 first-half group profits flat at 1.08 billion marks and said it expected stable profits for the year as a whole.
Its stock later came back to 90.55 in bourse trade, still against the overall market trend.
"The figures were disappointing simply because they were in line with expectations," said one trader, noting that the stock had risen strongly in recent days ahead of the results.
He added that a more positive profit outlook had been hoped for by some in the market.
Overall, a dollar that was above early morning lows but locked in narrow ranges just above 1.71 marks was also seen adding little impetus to the German equity market.
Preference shares in haircare products group Wella rose 38 marks to 1,000 as Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it had raised its recommendation in the stock to "overweight" from "neutral".
Wella said on Tuesday it expected 1997 net profits to climb 25 percent, with sales up seven percent.

Airline Lufthansa continued to rise as dealers cited strong technical factors and a general positive mood surrounding recent fundamentals in the stock, notably its continuing restructuring to boost profits.
It gained 50 pfennigs to 23.75 marks by 0815 GMT.
Auto shares were mostly higher as dealers said their rally, recently interrupted by a small pause, was now back on track.
BMW gained 28.50 marks to 1,397.50, Daimler rose 2.85 marks to 130.75 and Volkswagen was up 23 marks at 1,086.
